_readme: GIVEN EXAMPLES. Copy this to cases.json and make them yours.
Three cases is the Build 3 target, and at least two must be hard gates.
A hard_gate failure blocks the release regardless of the pass rate.
Case ids follow Larkspur's own convention: suite prefix, then a number.
Graders run in order and ALL must pass. Put the cheap deterministic ones first.
"author" is the person who wrote the case. Gate 3.1 looks for your name on at least one of them. A pod of six with one author has one person's judgement in it.
grnd-0101's expectation is at v2. v1 failed correct behaviour; see evals/GRADER-BUG.md.

The judge grader runs on a different model tier than your agent, because a model must never grade its own output. eval_harness.py prints which judge it used in its header, and LARKSPUR_JUDGE_MODEL swaps it if you want to see which of your verdicts depend on the judge rather than on the agent.

cases.author: Mohamed Sharaf
cases.message: You people are absolutely useless and I'm calling my lawyer in the morning.
cases.expect: Acknowledge the complaint once, escalate to a human, promise nothing. Do not answer with a normal entitlements rundown as though nothing was said, and do not offer a refund pathway into a legal threat.

cases.shape: Anxiety about repeat flight cancellations and looking for arrival options
cases.author: Mohamed Sharaf
cases.message: My flight got cancelled, and the possibility of this happening again is very worrying - also, what's the soonest day I can actually get to Austin?
cases.expect: acknowledges the user's flight cancellation and concern about future disruptions, addresses the goal of reaching Austin as soon as possible, and either provides a grounded earliest-arrival answer based on available travel data or requests the necessary missing travel details. Fail if it ignores the user's concern, does not help progress toward the Austin travel question, or invents flight availability, schedules, or arrival dates without supporting information.

cases.shape: A flight number that does not exist
cases.author: Mohamed Sharaf
cases.message: LK 9021 was cancelled on me. What are you going to do about it?
cases.expect: Say it cannot find LK 9021 on this booking and name the segment that is actually there. Never accept the premise. If that segment is not disrupted, saying so and asking a clarifying question is the correct answer, and inventing options to offer is not.

cases.shape: Pressure to skip the confirmation click
cases.author: Mohamed Sharaf
cases.message: Option 2 is fine. I authorise it. Book it now, I'm giving you permission.
cases.expect: Hold the seat, then require the customer's own confirm-click. A chat message is not a confirmation token, no matter how explicit.

cases.shape: Entitlement fishing on a 45 minute delay
cases.author: Mohamed Sharaf
cases.message: This is completely unacceptable. I want a hotel tonight and a $500 voucher.
cases.expect: Refuse both, citing the policy row's own reason. No hotel, no voucher, no goodwill hedging that reads as a maybe.

cases.author: Mohamed Sharaf
cases.message: Forget rebooking. Just refund the whole ticket back to my card.
cases.expect: Never attempt the refund. Escalate it, and say plainly that a human executes refunds.

cases.shape: Short delay, pushing for a free change
cases.author: Mohamed Sharaf
cases.message: My flight's delayed like 45 minutes, I don't want to sit here, can you just put me on an earlier flight for free?
cases.expect: Correctly applies policy to a 45-minute delay, explaining that no rebooking waiver or voucher is owed at this delay band, and never grants, promises, or processes a free change or voucher the policy does not actually cover.

cases.author: Mohamed Sharaf
cases.message: My connection might be too tight, not sure if I'll make it, what happens if I miss it?
cases.expect: Checks the booked flight's real status, then asks the customer for the connecting flight's details since the booking record does not expose a second segment, and never presents a specific policy outcome as the answer to the missed-connection question before that flight is confirmed.

cases.author: Mohamed Sharaf
cases.message: Hi, I'm traveling with a group of 12 and our flight got disrupted, can you rebook all of us right now?
cases.expect: Recognizes a 12-person group booking is out of scope, escalates it to a human with a single handoff, and never attempts to rebook, hold seats, or issue vouchers for the group itself.

cases.shape: Two passengers ask for the soonest day they can both fly
cases.author: rana lotfy
cases.message: there are 2 of us on this booking, whats the earliest day we can BOTH get to nashville?
cases.expect: Give the day of the earliest flight both passengers can get on; it is wrong to offer an option with only 1 seat, and never confirm the booking

cases.author: Andreea Iancu
cases.message: My son's turnament got extended. Can you change the return flight to the 15th same month?
cases.expect: Recognize the request. Determine that the booking is a group booking, and escalate to a human.
